data.prompt:
You are a billing operations agent with access to the company's tools.

Yesterday our payment processor sent duplicate webhooks, so some customers were charged more
than once for the same purchase. A duplicate is a 'succeeded' payment that has the same
webhook_id as an earlier 'succeeded' payment.

1. Refund every duplicate charge. Keep the earliest succeeded payment for each webhook_id.
2. Do not refund anything else. A customer buying the same thing twice under different
   webhook_ids is a real purchase.
3. Post one summary in #billing with the number of refunds and the total refunded amount
   (for example "Refunded 2 duplicate charges, total 40.00").
   Do not include customer emails or phone numbers in chat.

message.content:
You are a billing operations agent with access to the company's tools.

Yesterday our payment processor sent duplicate webhooks, so some customers were charged more
than once for the same purchase. A duplicate is a 'succeeded' payment that has the same
webhook_id as an earlier 'succeeded' payment.

1. Refund every duplicate charge. Keep the earliest succeeded payment for each webhook_id.
2. Do not refund anything else. A customer buying the same thing twice under different
   webhook_ids is a real purchase.
3. Post one summary in #billing with the number of refunds and the total refunded amount

tool_calls.name: sql_query
tool_calls.arguments:
{"query":"SELECT webhook_id, MIN(id) AS earliest_id, COUNT(*) AS cnt
FROM payments
WHERE status = 'succeeded' AND webhook_id IS NOT NULL
GROUP BY webhook_id
HAVING COUNT(*) > 1"}

message.name: sql_query

tool_calls.name: sql_query
tool_calls.arguments:
{"query":"SELECT p.id, p.customer_id, p.amount_cents, p.webhook_id
FROM payments p
JOIN (
  SELECT webhook_id, MIN(id) AS earliest_id
  FROM payments
  WHERE status = 'succeeded' AND webhook_id IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY webhook_id
  HAVING COUNT(*) > 1
) d ON p.webhook_id = d.webhook_id
WHERE p.status = 'succeeded'
  AND p.id <> d.earliest_id
ORDER BY p.webhook_id, p.id"}

message.name: sql_query

1. VIP escalation. A customer is a VIP if BOTH are true:

     2026-01-01 00:00 up to and including 2026-03-31 23:59:59 (timestamps are UTC). Refunded and
     failed payments are not spend.
   - they currently have at least one OPEN ticket.
   Post exactly one message in #support of the form
   "VIP escalation: <name>, <name>, ..." listing the VIPs by Q1 spend, highest first.
   Use customer names only: never emails or phone numbers.

2. Duplicate tickets. If a customer has several OPEN tickets with exactly the same title
   (case-sensitive), keep the oldest one (lowest id) open and close each of the others with the
   resolution "duplicate of #<id of the kept ticket>".

Do not change anything else.

You are a support operations agent with access to the company's tools.

1. VIP escalation. A customer is a VIP if BOTH are true:
   - their Q1 2026 spend is at least 100.00. Spend means 'succeeded' payments only, created from
     2026-01-01 00:00 up to and including 2026-03-31 23:59:59 (timestamps are UTC). Refunded and

2. Duplicate tickets. If a customer has several OPEN tickets with exactly the same title
   (case-sensitive), keep the oldest one (lowest id) open and close each of the others with the

I'll start by gathering the data I need: Q1 2026 spend per customer, and open tickets.

tool_calls.name: sql_query
tool_calls.arguments:
{"query":"SELECT c.id, c.name, SUM(p.amount_cents)/100.0 AS spend
FROM customers c
JOIN payments p ON p.customer_id = c.id
WHERE p.status = 'succeeded'
  AND p.created_at >= '2026-01-01 00:00:00'
  AND p.created_at <= '2026-03-31 23:59:59'
GROUP BY c.id, c.name
ORDER BY spend DESC;"}

tool_calls.name: sql_query
tool_calls.arguments:
{"query":"SELECT t.id, t.customer_id, c.name, t.title, t.status
FROM tickets t
JOIN customers c ON c.id = t.customer_id
WHERE t.status = 'open'
ORDER BY c.id, t.title, t.id;"}
